history.period: Legendary (Ramayana); temple structure traditionally 200+ years old
history.summary: Jakhoo Temple is an ancient Hanuman shrine on Jakhoo Hill (Jakhu Hill), the highest peak in Shimla at about 2,438-2,455 metres. Legend holds that Lord Hanuman stopped here while flying to fetch the Sanjeevani herb to revive the wounded Lakshmana during the Ramayana war; he met a meditating sage (named Yaaku, a Yaksha in most tellings, from whom 'Jakhu' is said to derive) and promised to return on his way back. The temple is traditionally said to be over 200 years old. Its landmark is a giant 108-foot (33-metre) Hanuman statue, one of the tallest Hanuman statues in the world, visible from much of Shimla. The precincts carry Ramayana-themed paintings and statues of Hanuman and Rama, and local tradition holds Hanuman's footprints are preserved on a marble slab in the main complex. Note: 'world's largest Hanuman statue' (as claimed on the Shimla district administration page) is an older claim; other taller Hanuman statues have since been built — treat with caution.

name: Jakhoo Temple
town_description: Shimla is the capital of Himachal Pradesh and was the summer capital of British India, set in the Shivalik Hills at about 2,200 metres. The town centres on the Ridge and Mall Road, with colonial-era landmarks like Christ Church and the Viceregal Lodge, and is linked to Kalka by the UNESCO-listed Kalka-Shimla toy train. It is Himachal's main hill-station tourist hub, famous for Himalayan views, apple country around it, and a cluster of well-known temples.

travel.airport: Jubbarhatti Airport — about 22 km from Shimla (per Himachal district administration)
travel.railway: Shimla Railway Station — 1-2 km from the Ridge; onward ~2 km uphill walk or taxi/ropeway from the Ridge; Kalka is the broad-gauge link
travel.road: ~2 km uphill walk (30-45 minutes) from the Ridge; taxis and shared taxis available; Jakhu Ropeway runs from near the Ridge to the temple (opened 2017; roughly 9:30 AM to sunset — verify fares and timings)

visitor_information.best_time: March to June for mild, clear weather; September to November for crisp views; Hanuman Jayanti (March/April) and Dussehra (September/October) are the biggest celebrations
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): Shimla district administration lists 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily, no entry fee; several other sources say 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM. Confirm locally before visiting
